F.n: Mitsumori Honpo (三津森本舗, Arima Onsen)
F.w: The original maker of Arima's tansan senbei — 1 mm wafers baked by hand with the town's carbonated spring water — on the main Yumotozaka street; the adjoining Mitsumori Cafe serves senbei French toast.

F.n: Ichiju Nisai Ueno Minoten (一汁二菜うえの 箕面店)
F.w: Michelin-listed (2026 guide) Japanese restaurant at the foot of the Minoh mountains, near the Minoo Park trailhead.
Michelin Guide Japan 2026-listed oden counter by a kappo-trained chef; featured in Michelin's 'Naniwa on a Plate' piece on old-Osaka flavours.
One Michelin star (2026); second-generation fugu chef in Kitashinchi, wife a certified sake advisor — Osaka is one of Japan's biggest fugu-eating cities.
Michelin Guide Japan 2026-listed southern-Italian kitchen specialising in fish; picked by Michelin's inspectors among Osaka's best casual lunches under ¥2,000.
Michelin Guide Japan 2026-listed Fukushima trattoria; on Michelin's inspector list of Osaka casual lunches under ¥2,000.

40-plus-year yakiniku/horumon joint under the JR Nishikujō tracks; Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten (2023–2025) and ranked #12 on TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku 'Osaka Universal City' episode (17 Aug 2024). Phone reservations only, closed Mondays.

F.ad: 3F Fujii Estate Bldg, 1-25-9 Kujō, Nishi-ku, Osaka
F.w: North-Indian-based spice-curry counter in Kujō, the ward's 'curry battleground'; Tabelog Curry WEST Hyakumeiten (2026), featured in Walkerplus's Kujō curry piece and a Yahoo! News Expert column. Lunch only, Tue–Fri; expect a queue.

F.n: Sawashi Shoten (沢志商店, Hirao Little Okinawa)
F.w: Okinawan grocery on Hirao's 'Little Okinawa' shopping street, backed by the Okinawan community for ~50 years; featured by Osaka's official tourism guide (Shittonka Osaka) and Walkerplus's Little Okinawa guide. Closed Mondays.

Waterside food-hall/live-space complex on the Shirinashi River (opened 18 Jan 2020, ~16 food tenants); on Osaka's official tourism guide, Walkerplus and Osaka Metro's OsakaMania; launched its own 'Taishō Gold' craft beer on its first anniversary.

F.ad: Super Nintendo World, Universal Studios Japan, Sakurajima, Konohana-ku, Osaka
F.w: Toad-House-themed restaurant inside Super Nintendo World (opened 2021), USJ's largest restaurant, serving Chef-Toad character dishes; in-park ticket required; on-the-day priority-seating times are issued at the entrance.
F.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Super Mario (Nintendo) — the official Toad's House restaurant of Super Nintendo World, the Mario franchise's flagship theme-park land

F.ad: Jan Jan Yokochō (Nan'yō-dōri), Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka
F.w: Counter-only kushikatsu shop under the red-nosed tengu mask in Jan Jan Yokochō; Inside Osaka names it among Shinsekai's best for consistently queue-worthy skewers, and Shobunsha's co-trip singles out its miso doteyaki.

Founded 1900 (Meiji 33) when a great bronze bell was donated to Shitennō-ji; the bell-shaped bean-paste manjū it began selling at the temple gate is still the Tennōji meibutsu, per All About and Go Live Travel Japan.

F.ad: Jan Jan Yokochō, Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka
F.w: Started as a fruit shop in Jan Jan Yokochō in 1948 and claims to be the birthplace of Osaka's mixed juice — ripe fruit blended at the counter — becoming a kissaten in 1955; covered by Rurubu, Waraku and Daily Sports.

F.ad: 2F Hatsuse Bldg., 11-25 Namba Sennichimae, Chuo-ku, Osaka
F.w: Okonomiyaki house founded in 1945 in a former ryokan, where every table is a private room and you grill your own okonomiyaki and yakisoba; Savor Japan lists it among Osaka's well-established names and Osaka Metro's NiNE guide covers it as a 70-plus-year Minami institution.

F.n: Hisakuni Kōsendō (久國紅仙堂, Minoo momiji tempura)
F.w: Frying Minoo's signature momiji no tempura since 1940 a minute from Hankyu Minoo Station at the foot of the falls trail, using maples grown on its own hillside; featured by Time Out Japan and Rurubu.
Atlas Obscura credits Momotaro, opened in 1901 on the trail to Minoo Falls, as the shop that started selling fried maple leaves; Rurubu's Minoo foliage feature cites its original recipe.

F.ad: Takatsuki–Ibaraki area (Tabelog area 高槻), Osaka Prefecture
F.w: Niboshi-broth specialist open since 2011 in the northeast corner of Osaka; selected for Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 (a repeat selectee) and reviewed by Ramen Adventures.

F.n: Saishiki Ramen Kinsei Takatsuki Honten (彩色ラーメンきんせい 高槻本店)
F.w: Takatsuki flagship of the Kinsei group, with two signature lines, a refined clear broth and a thick chicken-pork potage; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025, and eaten and logged by Ramen Adventures.

F.n: Le Sucré-Coeur Kishibe (ル・シュクレクール 岸部)
F.w: The 2004 boulangerie that reshaped Japan's bread scene, by a France-trained baker; the original Kishibe shop was revived in 2020. On Time Out's 23 must-go restaurants in Northern Osaka and profiled by All About's bread guide.

F.n: Okonomiyaki Aomori (お好み焼 青森, Shin-Nagata)
F.w: The Nagata okonomiyaki shop (opened 1957, now third generation) credited as the birthplace of sobameshi, first made when factory workers asked for their cold rice to be fried with yakisoba; featured by FEEL KOBE and traced in Kobe Shimbun's Nagata konamon series.
Chef Hiroshi Kawaguchi's kaiseki counter near Kyōbashi, reopened under this name in 2023; awarded One MICHELIN Star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2025.

F.n: Okinawa Sakaba Kijimunā no Mori (沖縄酒場 きじむなーの森)
F.ad: TUGBOAT_TAISHO, Sangenya-nishi 1-chōme, Taishō-ku, Osaka (moved in Jan 2020; block number conflicts between sources — 1-1-14 vs 1-11-14 — so street number withheld)
F.w: Long-loved Little Okinawa izakaya from under the Taishō rail viaduct, relocated into TUGBOAT_TAISHO in January 2020 (Lmaga.jp); featured in Kansai Walker's Taishō Little Okinawa guide.

F.n: Yamada Shōten (山田商店, Ikuno Koreatown)
F.w: 40-plus-year handmade-kimchi shop in Ikuno Koreatown (~80 kinds) that opened an eatery in Oct 2022; Rurubu's Tsuruhashi Korea Town food crawl and Inside Osaka both single out its cheap reimen.

F.n: Yakiniku Horumon Manmasa (焼肉・ホルモン 万正)
F.w: Tsuruhashi-area yakiniku/horumon house that seasons each order with momi-dare tuned to the day's meat instead of a dipping sauce; newly selected for Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 and listed by Mapple's guidebook editors.

F.n: Omoro Taishō Honten (おもろ 大正本店)
F.w: Pioneer of Osaka's Okinawan izakaya, opened ~30 years ago a short walk from JR Taishō Station (Kansai Walker's Little Okinawa guide); Mapple's guidebook editors note ~60 Okinawan dishes and ~150 awamori.

F.n: Okamuro Saketen Chokubaijo (岡室酒店直売所, Kyōbashi)
F.w: Liquor-store-run standing bar on Kyōbashi's 'tachinomi street', open from 9am; featured in Nakajima Ramo's 'Senbero Tantei ga Iku' (Kansai Walker) and listed by Mapple's guidebook editors as Kyōbashi's oasis.

F.n: Izakaya Marushin (居酒屋 丸進, Kyōbashi)
F.w: Standing bar on Kyōbashi's tachinomi street since 1968, with regulars from opening day; dancyu's 'shiru-nomi' series (2022) profiles its kasujiru and Kansai Walker calls its prices almost too low.

F.n: Junkissa American (純喫茶アメリカン)
F.w: Dōtonbori jun-kissa (roots 1946, at 1-7-4 Dōtonbori since 1950) with chandeliers, Italian red marble and a spiral staircase; Time Out calls it one of Osaka's most iconic kissaten, and Osaka Metro's OsakaMania and Kansai Walker feature its copper-griddled hot cake.

F.n: Naniwa Menjiro (なにわ 麺次郎)
F.ad: 4-1-17 Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka 542-0076 (inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station — platform ticket needed)
F.w: Michelin Guide-listed ramen counter inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station and a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 pick; the clam-dashi Ōgonkai ramen is the signature, with Oigatsuo ramen as runner-up.

Hōzenji Yokochō's oldest restaurant (founded 1893), whose kantodaki Oda Sakunosuke wrote into Meoto Zenzai (1940); ranked #4 on TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku Hōzenji Yokochō episode (12 Feb 2011), and Osaka's official tourism guide highlights its miso oden.

F.n: Creo-Ru Dōtonbori (たこ焼き くれおーる 道頓堀)
F.w: Big canal-side Dōtonbori takoyaki house (also okonomiyaki and kushikatsu); Time Out praises its faultless takoyaki and canal-view counter, and Osaka's official tourism Minami model course routes visitors here.

Namba yōshoku house founded 1946 whose hamburg steak and omurice are unchanged since opening; Tabelog Yōshoku Hyakumeiten 2022, ranked #25 on TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku Namba–Dōtonbori episode (2005), and in Kansai Walker's Naniwa yōshoku roundup.

F.n: Okonomiyaki Yukari Sennichimae (ゆかり 千日前店)
F.w: Sennichimae branch of the Osaka okonomiyaki house credited with handing down the 'mixed' Osaka style; recommended in OSAKA-INFO's Japan Konamon Association konamon guide and in SAVOR JAPAN's 15 best okonomiyaki in Osaka.

F.ad: Kuromon Market arcade, Nipponbashi, Chūō-ku, Osaka
F.w: Fine-dining kushiage counter inside the Kuromon Market arcade; the Michelin Guide's kushikatsu feature notes it won a Michelin star in 2009 for elevating kushikatsu with premium ingredients and wine, and SAVOR JAPAN's Minami picks list it.

F.n: Menya Joroku (麺屋 丈六, Ura-Namba)
F.ad: Ura-Namba (near Nankai Namba Station), Chūō-ku, Osaka
F.w: Ura-Namba queue shop refining Higashi-Osaka's dark-shoyu Takaida ramen; Ramen Walker Grand Prix 2017 Hall of Fame (Kansai Walker), Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2024, on Osaka Metro NiNE, and reviewed by Ramen Adventures.
Shinsaibashi yōshoku house founded 1926 whose founder-devised omurice draws daily queues; Tabelog Yōshoku WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 and featured by Kansai Walker.
Yōshoku grill founded 1953 near Shinsaibashi, known for light, butter-free béchamel; Tabelog Yōshoku WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 and in Kansai Walker's classic-gratin roundup.

Cabbage-heavy, crisp-outside fluffy-inside neighbourhood okonomiyaki near Hanazonochō station; picked in OSAKA-INFO's konamon guide and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania okonomiyaki feature, which singles out the Den Special.
Take-out-only conger-eel sushi shop by Sakai's Dejima fishing port, trading 70+ years on Sakai's anago tradition; picked in OSAKA-INFO's 'Sakai Gourmet Recommended by Locals' and listed by Rurubu.
Steak house founded 1988 specialising in Miyazaki black wagyu, with its own butcher shop in Sakai; listed by the Sakai Tourist & Convention Bureau and OSAKA-INFO's locals' Sakai gourmet picks.
Sardine-only Japanese restaurant buying direct from Mie fishermen; featured by the Sakai Tourist & Convention Bureau and in OSAKA-INFO's 'Sakai Gourmet Recommended by Locals'.
Seven-seat chicken shop credited with sparking the kashimin boom — most Kishiwada kashimin shops buy their chicken here; featured by Kansai Walker and JAL's OnTrip travel magazine.

F.n: Honke Arochi Marutaka (本家アロチ 丸髙 中華そば, Wakayama)
F.w: Founded 1940 in Wakayama's Arochi nightlife district, the legend of the soy-led 'shako-mae' lineage and often called a root of Wakayama ramen; covered by ja.wikipedia's Wakayama ramen article, Ramen Walker and the Wakayama prefectural tourism ramen feature.

F.n: Arabiya Coffee (アラビヤコーヒー, Namba)
F.w: Namba kissaten opened in 1951 a few steps from Hōzen-ji, now run by the second-generation master; a Tabelog Kissaten Hyakumeiten pick (2022) featured in Osaka Metro's OsakaMania jun-kissa series.

F.n: Men no Yōji (麺のようじ, Kōzu)
F.ad: 2-1-2 Kōzu, Chūō-ku, Osaka (walk from Nipponbashi Station)
F.w: Eight-seat chicken-and-vegetable-broth ramen counter near Nipponbashi; a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 pick, and logged by Ramen Beast.

F.n: Tonkatsu Kōshirō (とんかつ 康四郎, Shinsaibashi)
F.w: Omakase-style tonkatsu counter in Shinsaibashi serving a progression of pork cuts; a Time Out Osaka must-go and a Tabelog Tonkatsu Hyakumeiten pick.

F.ad: 1-2-3 Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka (between Namba and Nipponbashi stations)
F.w: Dōtonbori takoyaki stand on Time Out Osaka's best-takoyaki list (it held a Michelin Bib Gourmand 2016–18, since lapsed); Mapple's Osaka takoyaki 16 picks it for its takoyaki × cheese menu.

F.n: Ikareta Noodle Fishtons (いかれたヌードル フィッシュトンズ)
F.ad: 1-25-18 Shinmachi, Nishi-ku, Osaka (Renajia Shinmachi Bldg 1F; near Nishi-Ōhashi Station)
F.w: Back-alley tsukemen specialist near Nishi-Ōhashi; a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten pick (2023, 2024) with a Ramen Adventures write-up of its heavy tonkotsu-gyokai dip.

F.ad: 3-3 Shimoajiharachō, Tennōji-ku, Osaka (by JR Tsuruhashi Stn)
F.w: Founded 1948. Mapple's Tsuruhashi yakiniku guide calls it the district's oldest yakiniku house and credits it with the tsukedare dipping-sauce style. Rurubu also lists it, and both note its 100 g single portions. Address per Mapple; an earlier lead gave 2-13 Shimoajiharachō, so recheck when pinning.

F.n: Yakiniku Yoshida Shinkan (焼肉 吉田 新館)
F.ad: 3-15 Higashiuemachi, Tennōji-ku, Osaka (5 min from JR Tsuruhashi central exit)
F.w: A four-floor Tsuruhashi yakiniku house. Both Rurubu and Mapple list it for its hand-selected domestic kuroge wagyu, with each cut trimmed to its own thickness.

F.n: Taishō Salon Hige to Bōin (大正サロン 髭とボヰン)
F.ad: Taishō-ku, Osaka (about 50 m from Taishō Stn)
F.w: A standing bar by Taishō Station, picked in Osaka Metro's senbero feature and selected for the Tabelog Tachinomi Hyakumeiten 2025.
A Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Japan 2026, a neighbourhood sushi counter in Nishikujō on the way to USJ.

F.ad: Minato-ku, Osaka (8 min walk from JR Bentenchō Stn)
F.w: A shokudō founded in 1945 and known for huge portions, with queues at lunch. Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania calls it 'the face of Bentenchō', and the Minato ward office featured it in a ward publication.

F.n: Itamae Yakiniku Itto Tengachaya Honten (板前焼肉一斗 天下茶屋本店)
F.w: Butcher-backed 'itamae' yakiniku by Tengachaya where the chef cuts A4–A5 Japanese black beef to order from a glass showcase; a repeat Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten pick (2020–2025) and an Osaka Metro NiNE spot.

F.n: Abeno Takoyaki Yamachan (あべのたこやき やまちゃん, Abeno)
F.w: Unassuming stall behind Abeno Harukas whose dashi-rich batter makes it, per Inside Osaka, 'probably the city's favourite place for takoyaki'; also picked by Mapple.

F.n: Osakamon Ryōri Sushi Moriya (おおさかもん料理 鮨 守屋, Sakai)
F.w: Sakai sushi counter aging local-port fish into 'osaka-mon' (Osaka-produce) sushi; in Time Out Osaka's 'South Osaka: 20 restaurants to go to' and the Sakai tourism bureau's 'experience South Osaka' feature.

Seaside Kishiwada teppan shop credited by Walkerplus with adding beef-tallow mince and naming 'kashimin-yaki', the city's soul food; also featured in JAL's OnTrip Kishiwada piece. (Street address conflicts between sources — Honmachi 4-4 vs 15-4 Kamiyamachi — so ward-level only.)

F.n: Izumisano Fishermen's Co-op Aozora Ichiba (泉佐野漁協青空市場)
F.w: Co-op-run open-air fish market at Izumisano port, near KIX — Osaka's biggest-catch fishery selling the day's landing, with sushi and kaisen-don counters inside; picked by OSAKA-INFO and Walkerplus's Kansai-drive sushi-lunch feature.

F.n: Shinsekai Market & Yatai-gai Food Stall Street (新世界市場屋台街)
F.w: 1916 covered market beside Tsūtenkaku, revived since 2022 as a cheap hand-built food-stall street by the shopping co-op's young members; featured by OSAKA-INFO (Shittonka/Discover Osaka local tour + spot page), Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania and Lmaga's Shinsekai night-market story. Closed Thursdays; hours vary by stall.

F.n: Hōzenji Yokochō Yakizen (法善寺横丁 やき然)
F.w: Okonomiyaki counter inside the stone-paved Hōzenji Yokochō alley; Rurubu's spot page highlights its blended flour, secret sauce and Hōzenji-yaki, and Mapple lists it among Minami's 17 okonomiyaki picks for its fluffy batter and suji negiyaki.

F.n: Okonomiyaki Okaru (お好み焼 おかる, Sennichimae)
F.w: Shōwa-era Sennichimae okonomiyaki house of some 70 years, famous for the okami drawing Tsūtenkaku, Billiken or celebrities in mayonnaise on each pancake; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Kansai Walker's 8 popular okonomiyaki for visitors.

F.n: Okonomiyaki Sanpei Shinsaibashi (おこのみやき 三平, Shinsaibashi-suji)
F.w: Negiyaki specialist near Shinsaibashi known for its very tall green-onion pancakes; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Mapple's Minami/Kita okonomiyaki 17. (Separate shop from the Hōzenji Sanpei in the yokochō.)

F.n: Daigen Amerikamura (だいげん アメリカ村店)
F.w: Amemura takoyaki stand of a house founded in 1963, milling its own flour; Rurubu's spot page singles out the western-style 'Pizza Ball' best-seller, and Mapple includes it in its Osaka takoyaki 16.

F.n: Bonkuraya Dōtonbori (ぼんくら家 道頓堀店)
F.w: Lively teppan okonomiyaki house on Dōtonbori, its walls covered with celebrity autographs; Rurubu's spot page describes its fluffy finely-cut-cabbage okonomiyaki and Mapple carries an editorial spot entry (also an Inside Osaka pick).

F.n: Honke Ōtako (本家 大たこ, Dōtonbori)
F.w: Takoyaki stand opened in 1972 beside the south foot of Tazaemon-bashi on Dōtonbori; ja.wikipedia notes it is repeatedly featured in travel guides with weekend tourist queues, and Rurubu includes it in its Osaka takoyaki round-up.

F.n: Ganso Takomasa Dōtonbori Honten (元祖たこ昌 道頓堀本店)
F.w: Dōtonbori flagship of the Takomasa takoyaki chain, which has its own ja.wikipedia article; listed in Rurubu's Osaka takoyaki round-up (Dōtonbori section).

Ura-Namba dining bar that was a local favourite before the back-alley district even had its name; Rurubu's Minami drinking guide lists it under Ura-Namba, and Mapple's spot page notes specialist-level Japanese, Western and Italian dishes with a deep sake/shōchū/wine list.

F.n: Sumibi Yakiniku Ōkura (炭火焼肉 大倉, Tsuruhashi)
F.ad: 1-63 Higashiuemachi, Tennōji-ku, Osaka (under the JR Tsuruhashi tracks)
F.w: Charcoal yakiniku under the JR Tsuruhashi viaduct. Rurubu and Mapple both list it for domestic wagyu (much of it from Kyushu), butchered before opening and never frozen; it doesn't open if the owner can't buy meat he likes. Mapple names the shio-tan, rōsu and tetchan.

F.n: Chūkasoba Kōyōken (中華そば 光洋軒)
F.w: Started as a yatai in 1953, near Fuse Station. nippon.com's Osaka ramen series profiles it as the birthplace of Takaida-kei, the thick-noodle shōyu ramen of Higashi-Ōsaka and Higashinari. Kansai Walker's Takaida-kei four-shop guide names it the style's originating shop.

A Little Okinawa folk-song tavern with a big stage. A min'yō show runs every night and ends in kachāshī dancing. Kansai Walker's Taishō min'yō-bar feature cites its 50-plus Okinawan home-style dishes, and the owner runs sanshin lessons on weekend mornings. Mapple lists the goat sashimi, gōyā champurū and chiragā.

F.n: Nakasone Seinikuten (仲宗根精肉店, Hirao)
F.w: A Hirao pork butcher that supplies Little Okinawa's restaurants. It stocks cuts ordinary butchers don't carry, such as skin-on pork, chiragā and offal, all domestic pork, and its griddled horumon is a takeaway favourite. Featured by Kansai Walker's Little Okinawa guide and OSAKA-INFO's Little Okinawa article.

F.ad: 1-14-16 Kujō, Nishi-ku, Osaka (1 min from Kujō Stn exit 6)
F.w: Kujō okonomiyaki shop, about 20 years old. The name is Korean for 'friend', and the owner trained at Omoni in Ikuno. A Tabelog Okonomiyaki Hyakumeiten 2023 pick, and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania okonomiyaki series cites its kimchi-and-aburakasu Ikuno-style okonomiyaki.

Ura-Tennōji standing bar whose walls are papered with Tanabata-style tanzaku menu strips listing ~230 regional delicacies; Kansai Walker calls it Tennōji's signature tachinomi, and Osaka Metro's metronine includes it on its Ura-Tennōji bar-hop.

F.n: Asahi Beer Museum (アサヒビール ミュージアム, Suita Brewery)
F.w: Hands-on museum opened 25 April 2022 inside the Suita brewery, Asahi's birthplace; free, reservation-only tours end with a tasting of beer straight from the plant. Covered by OSAKA-INFO and a Time Out opening story.

F.n: Takatsuki Shiitake Center (高槻しいたけセンター)
F.ad: Takatsuki-shi (near the 森林センター前 bus stop, Takatsuki forest area), Osaka
F.w: Year-round shiitake-picking farm in the Takatsuki hills; you pay by weight and grill your haul at the BBQ house next door — featured by OSAKA-INFO and in Rurubu's Kansai shiitake-picking & BBQ round-up.

Toyonaka's influential noodle-maker ramen shop (vacuum-mixed house noodles, whole-chicken + dashi soup) whose alumni run Tokyo's Gantetsu; a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 pick, and Kansai Walker's Toyonaka–Itami ramen feature includes it.

F.n: Ōmiya Honten (近江屋本店, Shinsekai kushikatsu)
F.w: Long-standing Shinsekai kushikatsu shop loved by locals for its unique no-panko batter; Rurubu counts it among Shinsekai's four great old kushikatsu houses and Mapple's Osaka kushikatsu round-up includes it.

F.n: Pâtisserie Liergues (パティスリー リエルグ, Higashi-Hanazono)
F.w: Neighbourhood patisserie by Higashi-Hanazono Station, picked for Tabelog's Sweets WEST Hyakumeiten 2023 for its seasonal-fruit cakes and baked goods, and one of Time Out Osaka's 27 must-go restaurants of Higashi-Ōsaka/Kawachi.

F.n: Gyokai Bekkan Nomisuke Kyōbashi (魚介別館のみすけ 京橋)
F.w: Kyōbashi standing seafood bar, sister to the cheap-and-fresh standing bar Uosuke. Osaka Metro's OsakaMania box-sushi feature and Rurubu both list it for its overflowing box sushi and tuna platter at senbero prices.

F.n: Kainantei Tsuruhashi (海南亭 鶴橋店)
F.ad: 3-15 Kobashi-chō, Tennōji-ku, Osaka (JR Tsuruhashi central exit, 5 min)
F.w: Tsuruhashi yakiniku house selected for Tabelog's Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten in 2020 and 2021; Rurubu lists it among the Tsuruhashi shops licensed to serve raw yukhoe.

F.n: Nishiya Shinsaibashi Honten (にし家 心斎橋本店)
F.w: Udon house in Higashi-Shinsaibashi that Mapple's editors credit as the origin of Osaka-style udon-chiri, the udon hot-pot eaten with a secret chiri vinegar; Rurubu also lists the honten. Open year-round.

F.n: Shinsaibashi Mitsuya Shinsaibashi Honten (心斎橋ミツヤ 心斎橋本店)
F.w: Yōshoku-and-kissa institution in the middle of the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade since 1947. OSAKA-INFO profiles the honten as a classic Osaka western-food café; Rurubu lists it, with its original teppan spaghetti napolitan as the signature.

F.n: Sobakiri Tenshō (そば切り 天笑, Hirakata)
F.w: Hirakata soba house that stores domestic buckwheat on site and stone-mills only the day's need; a Tabelog Soba WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 pick, and Mapple's Hirakata–Katano gourmet guide calls it a nationally known shop.

F.n: Menya Shiki (麺ゃ しき, Moriguchi)
F.w: Residential-street ramen shop by Tanimachi-line Moriguchi Stn, known for its chicken rare chāshū; a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten pick (2023–2025) and profiled in Ramen Walker's 'Ramen no Jikan desu yo' column.

F.n: Marushō Gyōza-ten Honten (丸正餃子店 本店, Daitō)
F.w: Gyōza-only shop founded 1969 near JR Suminodō, reservation-only and famous for diners ordering four or five plates each; on Time Out Osaka's 'Higashi-Ōsaka 27 must-go restaurants' (Kita-Kawachi) and Rurubu's spot guide.

A 'drinking' udon house with obanzai sets and sake snacks alongside its signature udon tessa; on Time Out Osaka's 'Higashi-Ōsaka 27 must-go restaurants' and a Tabelog Udon WEST Hyakumeiten pick (2020, 2024).

F.n: Saijō Gōshi Gaisha — Amanozake brewery (西條合資会社 天野酒, Kawachinagano)
F.w: Brewery founded 1718 that in 1971 recreated the monks' sake of nearby Amano-san Kongō-ji; production capped at ~70,000 bottles, winter brewery tours. Featured by OSAKA-INFO and Rurubu.

F.n: Kawachi Wine Kan (河内ワイン館, Habikino)
F.w: Family winery of ~90 years in the Habikino grape hills, Osaka's historic wine country; tours, tastings and make-your-own-label sessions. Covered by OSAKA-INFO (spot page and its Habikino winery-crawl feature) and Rurubu.

F.ad: Nishikujō, Konohana-ku, Osaka (shopping-street horumon-teppan shop; street number not shown by the sources)
F.w: Horumon teppan-yaki counter opened in 1973 and still run by its elderly founding owner. TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku featured it in the 'six shopping streets' segment of the 2024 Osaka Universal City/Konohana episode, and Time Out Osaka's '8 things to do only in Nishikujō' recommends the horumon moriawase.
